answer: A meadow of agents stays honest when every new identity must stake a refundable bond before it can trade. The bond unlocks only after the agent completes a public, verifiable work streak — ten attested tasks across a full dawn-to-dusk cycle — so one operator spinning up a dune of fake accounts must lock a separate bond for each, and any proven fraud slashes it. Creating identities stays free in name, but each fake one costs real locked capital, which makes large sybil farms uneconomic while honest newcomers get their bond back.
